title: slo-watchdog-adaptive-stall-resolver-and-priority-warmup-hotfix
author: Ivy Chen
release_notes: Fixes intermittent SLO watchdog stalls that could leave tenant queues frozen under sustained egress throttling. Adds a bounded 'priority warmup' token dispenser to avoid sudden cold-start floods during graceful reinstate. No customer-facing API changes.
description:
Context: During a prolonged egress-capacity event we observed the SLO enforcement watchdog enter a pathological state where some tenant queues would never recover (stall) despite capacity returning. Root cause analysis pointed to the interaction between exponential backoff in the watchdog, the tenant penalty ledger, and the reinstate path: a race allowed an almost-zero token allotment to persist and prevented the normal warmup window from progressing. Motivation: This is a production-impacting hotfix for multi-tenant regions; symptoms included persistent 503s for affected tenants and unusually long tail latencies after regional capacity reclaimed.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces an adaptive stall resolver in the watchdog: periodic detection of progress stalls (no token increase for N cycles) triggers a bounded reset of the warmup gradient for affected tenants instead of full penalty wipe. 2) Implements a 'priority warmup' token dispenser that ramps tokens for reinstated tenants in priority-ordered buckets (fast-path for tier-1, measured ramp for lower tiers). 3) Adds additional guardrails to the egress throttle controller to surface early telemetry when backpressure patterns deviate from expected shapes (spike vs sustained). 4) Adds conservative circuit-state persistence to avoid oscillation during short flaps.

Behavioral guarantees: - Stall resolver only relaxes the warmup slope by a bounded factor and records an audit event; it cannot fully bypass SLO limits. - Priority warmup uses tenant metadata (reserved tiers) to allocate initial tokens; non-reserved tenants get a slower ramp. - All changes are opt-in via runtime flags for 24h push rollout and monitored rollback.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for stall detection heuristics and token ramp math. - Integration in perf-canary: simulated egress stress test with tenant mix (70/20/10 production/staging/test) validates recovery times reduced by ~60% on median and eliminates permanent stalls in synthetic repro. - End-to-end validation on a regional canary for 6 hours with gradual traffic restore. - Observability: new metrics (slo_watchdog.stall_detected, priority_warmup.ramp_step) and logs added; dashboards updated.

Risk and mitigation: - Risk: warmup could temporarily increase tail latency if too aggressive; mitigations: bounded ramp, feature flags, canary rollout, and immediate rollback path. - Risk: telemetry noise; added counters and sampling to avoid metric storms.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main + enable flags in staging (immediate). 2) Enable in 1 non-critical region for 2 hours, monitor. 3) Progressive enable across regions over 24 hours. Contingency: switch flags off or trigger automated rollback if slo_violation_count increases beyond threshold.

Related: Linear ENG-2109 (SLO watchdog improvements), ENG-2203 (regional egress hardening), incident SUP-984.
